common_name: President Giles Daylily (Fragrant Straw Self with Greenish-Yellow Throat, Parent of Double Love)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this fragrant evergreen diploid, registered by MacMillan in 1962, opens straw self flowers with a greenish-yellow throat in midseason.

directions: Registered by MacMillan in 1962 from a cross of an unnamed seedling and (Chetco x Dorcas), President Giles is a fragrant evergreen diploid daylily bearing a straw self flower with a greenish-yellow throat on 27-inch scapes with extended bloom habit that open in midseason. It carries no AHS awards of its own. B. Brown later used it alongside Double Decker as a parent of Double Love, an ancestor of the Ida Munson Award winner Mayor of Cornatzer. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous, fragrant flowering.

common_name: Double Decker Daylily (Light Gold Self Double, Parent of Double Love)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil; this evergreen double, registered by Thomas in 1962, opens light gold self flowers early in the midseason.

directions: Registered by Thomas in 1962 from a cross of an unnamed seedling and Cockade, Double Decker is an evergreen double daylily bearing a light gold self flower, about four and a half inches across on 26-inch scapes with nocturnal bloom habit that open early in the midseason. Thomas's own advertisement in The Daylily Journal noted that it always blooms double. It carries no AHS awards of its own. B. Brown later used it alongside President Giles as a parent of Double Love, an ancestor of the Ida Munson Award winner Mayor of Cornatzer. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain its double form.

common_name: Sanders Walker Daylily (Coral Rose with Orange Throat, Parent of Jock Randall)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant diploid, registered by Wood-W.T. in 1958, opens coral rose flowers with an orange throat in midseason.

directions: Registered by Wood-W.T. in 1958, Sanders Walker is a dormant diploid daylily bearing a coral rose flower with an orange throat on tall 36-inch scapes with extended bloom habit that open in midseason; no parentage was recorded at registration. It carries no AHS awards of its own. Peck later used it as a parent of Jock Randall, which went on to parent Illini Show Girl and, through that line, became an ancestor of the President's Cup winner Mary Alice. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Mary Mae Simon Daylily (Reblooming Cream Self with Green Throat, Parent of Mavis Smith)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this reblooming evergreen diploid, registered by MacMillan in 1965, opens cream self flowers with a green throat early in the season.

directions: Registered by MacMillan in 1965 from a cross of an unnamed seedling and Shalom, Mary Mae Simon is a reblooming evergreen diploid daylily bearing a cream self flower with a green throat, about five and a quarter inches across on 32-inch scapes with diurnal bloom habit that open early in the season. It carries no AHS awards of its own. G. Lenington later used it as a parent of Mavis Smith, which went on to parent Ed Marshall and, through that line, became an ancestor of the President's Cup winner Mary Alice. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to encourage repeat bloom.

common_name: Spring Waltz Daylily (Reblooming Orchid Self, Parent of Southern Heritage)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil; this reblooming evergreen diploid, registered by R.W. Munson in 1954, opens orchid self flowers on tall scapes in midseason.

directions: Registered by R.W. Munson in 1954 from a cross of Show Girl and (Mission Bells x Prima Donna), Spring Waltz is a reblooming evergreen diploid daylily bearing an orchid self flower on tall 44-inch scapes with diurnal bloom habit that open in midseason. It carries no AHS awards of its own. R.W. Munson later used it as a parent of Southern Heritage, which went on to parent Tim Tanner and, through that line, became an ancestor of the Lenington All-American Award winner Orange Velvet. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to encourage repeat bloom.

common_name: Strutter Daylily (Light Yellow Self, Parent of Solo)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant diploid, registered by Branch in 1957, opens light yellow self flowers in midseason.

directions: Registered by Branch in 1957, Strutter is a dormant diploid daylily bearing a light yellow self flower, about five inches across on 42-inch scapes with extended bloom habit that open in midseason; no parentage was recorded at registration. It carries no AHS awards of its own. Branch later used it as a parent of Solo, which went on to parent Jakarta and, through that line, became an ancestor of the Lenington All-American Award winner Orange Velvet. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.
